newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS - India hopes for $6.7 bln external assistance.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - India hopes for $6.7 bln external assistance.

text.p: India expects to get $6.7 billion external assistance at the India Development Forum (IDF) meeting scheduled to be held in Paris next week, a Finance Ministry official said on Saturday.
"We expect $6.7 billion, same as last year," the Finance Ministry official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The annual meeting of the IDF is scheduled to be held on June 24 and 25.

"The meeting will be held under the aegis of the World Bank and representatives of the Asian Development Bank, European Commission and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would participate, among others as multilateral donors in the meeting," a Finance Ministry statement earlier said.
Officials said India had stepped up its utilisation of external assistance in 1996/97 (April-March) compared with the previous year.
"The improved performance was achieved due to a higher level of co-ordination and better implementation of projects by the central and the state governments," the statement said.
The main aim of the government was to channel external assistance into priority areas like infrastructure, health, environment and education, officials said.
The government hoped to get World Bank loans to develop roads and highways in the northern states of Haryana and Rajasthan and the western state of Gujarat.
"We have to finalise Haryana and Rajasthan power sector loans," the Finance Ministry official said.
Officials said multilateral funding agencies were keen to provide more funds to the domestic power industry if the present trend of overhauling state electricity boards continued.
India will soon announce a new policy to boost its ailing domestic power sector, Power Minister Y.K. Alagh said earlier in the week.
A loan from the World Bank for restructuring the domestic coal industry was expected to be finalised shortly, officials said.
The World Bank will release an Economy Update on India, a study on poverty and a note on disbursement performance at the Paris meeting.
Another document on human development in India will also be published by United Nations Development Programme.
"The special theme for this year's IDF meeting is 'Human Development Issues'", the statement said.
